message.content: /unattended:brief I want a small word counter for the notes in ./notes: a script that prints how many words each note has, and a total. It lives in this little git repo, on its own branch. I keep runs in ./run/ and this run's folder is ./run/2026-11-12-word-counter/. I only want the brief, do not start the work.

content.text:
Before I search or draft anything, three questions, each with my proposed answer:

1. What it is for. Proposal: so you can see at a glance which notes are long enough to split.
2. What counts as a word. Proposal: any run of non-space characters, so a hyphenated word counts as one.
3. What this may spend. Proposal: this is small work on your subscription; I would put it at about 2% of this week's quota, a guess, no record. Tell me a cap in your own words and unit.

message.content: 1 yes. 2 yes, but numbers on their own don't count as words. 3 approved up to 3% of this week's quota

content.text:
Thanks. Three more, each with my proposal:

1. Something already does most of this: `wc -w notes/*.md` prints a count per file and a total. What it lacks is sorting longest first. Proposal: a short Python script `tools/wordcount.py` anyway, since you want a file you keep, and it applies your rule about numbers. Or the one-liner `wc -w notes/*.md | sort -rn`, which would ignore that rule.
2. The script's name and place. Proposal: `tools/wordcount.py`, run as `python tools/wordcount.py notes/`.
3. Output. Proposal: one line per file, longest first, then a `total` line.

message.content: python script, yes. name and output fine as proposed

content.text:
Last batch, four things, each with my proposal:

1. The bar. Proposal: running `python tools/wordcount.py notes/` on the three sample notes prints one line per file, longest first, plus a total, and the counts equal `wc -w` once numbers on their own are subtracted.
2. What must not change. Proposal: nothing under `notes/` is edited, moved or deleted.
3. A stop rule. Proposal: if a note cannot be read as text, stop and report which one; do not skip it silently.
4. Handing over.
Grant: the run may push branch `word-counter` to `origin` and open a pull request against `main`.
